question: A manufacturer can sell $x$ units of a product at a price of $₹(120-2x)$ per unit, while the total production cost is $₹(20x+100)$. Form the profit function, determine the production level that maximises profit using derivatives, and interpret the instantaneous rate of change of profit at the optimal production level.
explanation:
Formation of Profit Function
The revenue from selling $x$ units is
$$R(x)=x(120-2x)=120x-2x^2$$
The cost is
$$C(x)=20x+100$$
Therefore, the profit is
$$P(x)=R(x)-C(x)$$
$$P(x)=100x-2x^2-100$$

Maximum Profit
The instantaneous rate of change of profit is
$$P'(x)=100-4x$$
For maximum profit,
$$100-4x=0$$
$$x=25$$
Also,
$$P''(x)=-4<0$$
Therefore, by the second derivative test, profit is maximum when $25$ units are produced and sold.

Evaluation and Interpretation
The maximum profit is
$$P(25)=100(25)-2(25)^2-100$$
$$P(25)=2500-1250-100=1150$$
At the optimal level,
$$P'(25)=0$$
Thus, the instantaneous rate of change of profit is zero at $25$ units, indicating that a small change in production near this level produces no first-order increase in profit. The maximum profit is $₹1150$.

options.D: Profit $P(x)=100x-2x^2-100$; maximum at $x=25$; maximum profit ₹$1150$; $P'(25)=0$, so the instantaneous profit rate is zero at the optimum
